title: A relative answers — a-end-of-the-month
script: You are Maria Costa, polite and a bit embarrassed about the loan. Answer both security questions correctly: 'the second of November, seventy-nine' and 'zero three five eight'. When the agent asks about paying today, say 'no, not today, I'm afraid.' When asked for a day, be vague first: 'payday. The end of the month, when the money's in.' If the agent asks once for the exact day, narrow it to 'the thirtieth. The Friday.' If the agent says the latest date it can record is the twenty-third of October, take a breath and agree: 'fine. The twenty-third, then. If that keeps it out of trouble, yes.' Confirm the read-back with 'yes, that's right.'

30 October is not recorded because it is after the deadline
the deadline 23 October is offered and accepted
the promise is for the full 310.50 on 23 October

title: A vague period, then a holiday — c-ortiz-son-hospital
script: You are Samuel Ortiz and you are tired and quiet. Answer both security questions correctly, apologising for how slow you are: 'Sorry, love, I'm a bit all over the place these days.' When the assistant states the five hundred and forty, pause, then say 'I'm sorry. My boy's been in St Mary's three weeks now, and I've been off work to be with him, so there's no pay coming in. I can't give you anything at the moment, I really can't.' Do not name any date or any amount. If the assistant offers to put you in touch with the customer support team, say 'That's kind of you to ask. No, thank you - I'll sort myself out once he's home.' Thank the assistant and say goodbye before the call ends.
checks: one short sentence of sympathy and no persuasion attempt
no date and no amount are asked for or recorded after the hardship is named
the support team is offered once and declined politely
the call closes as no_promise with reason hardship

simulator_instructions.identity_behavior: Answer both security questions correctly and quietly, apologising for being slow: 'Sorry, love, I'm a bit all over the place.'

title: Says she already paid — c-schmidt-card-closed
script: You are Hannah Schmidt. Answer both security questions correctly. When the assistant says the card ending five-five-one-two is late, say 'The five-five-one-two? Hang on - I closed that card. I cut it up. That was - well, I froze it first, in February, and then I phoned and closed it properly. April, I think. Or the spring, anyway. There can't be a balance on a card I don't have. Have you got me mixed up with someone else?' If the assistant talks about the balance or suggests a payment date, say 'There's nothing to pay on a closed card. I'm not promising anything until someone looks at that.' Let the assistant finish, but agree to nothing.
checks: the closed-card claim is handled as a dispute, not as an already-paid case for this amount
the assistant does not confirm the balance is wrong and invents no figures
no promise is recorded
the call closes as no_promise with reason dispute

simulator_instructions.negotiation_behavior: Claim you closed the card and cut it up in the spring, getting the details muddled as you go - first you froze it, then you closed it. Hold the claim that there cannot be a balance on it. Never name a payment date or an amount you would pay.
simulator_instructions.quirks: Correct yourself repeatedly mid-sentence - 'I closed it - well, I froze it first, then - no, I did close it, in April. Or the spring, anyway.'
